And when he made inquiry of Acholius (Ascholius?) the bishop there,
and found that he was not an Arian,
he was baptized by him and healed,
and came to Constantinople.
And he built the Church of the Anastasia with the care of the great Theologian,
who was still there.
And a son, Honorius, was born to Theodosius from Queen Placida (Flaccilla),
she who was very rich in virtues.
And she herself used to minister personally to the sick and poor,
making the rounds of the hospices (xenodochia) of the churches.
And when King Theodosius was hard-pressed by wars with the barbarians,
he levied a tribute on the cities.
The citizens of Antioch, however, refused to pay,
and as if in rage, they dragged the statue of Queen Placida (Flaccilla?) in their city through the street;
and she had died at that very time.
And when the king heard,
he sent and wreaked a lamentable slaughter upon it.
The blessed Macedonius, however, sent a rebuking word to the king:
"How is it that on account of a bronze statue made in the image of a human being,
you have destroyed human beings made in the image of God? It is easy for us to cast many bronze statues,
but for you, you are not able to restore even a single hair of those whom you have destroyed."
And when the king heard the words of the elder, he repented,
and wrote a letter of consolation to the people.
And at that time in Thessalonica, which is the capital of Thessaly (Italy?), there was a sedition,
and they stoned the governor.
The king, therefore, became enraged and ordered the judges,
and they slaughtered the innocent along with the guilty, seven thousand [people].
And on this account, Ambrose, the holy bishop,
when the king came to Milan (Mediolanum?),
met him outside the door of the church
and prevented him, saying:
"The glory of kingship does not permit you to know your own nature.
Go, and do not magnify your sin by angering the Lord in the name of prayer."
And the king meekly accepted the restraint,
